conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived. We’ll use a short, well-studied tool called the Edinburgh Postpartum Depression Scale—EPDS for short. It’s simply ten questions about the past seven days; your answers are confidential and will help us understand what kind of support or resources would be most helpful for you right now. There are no right or wrong answers, and you can share as much or as little as feels comfortable. Whenever you’re ready, we can begin.

To start, how have you been feeling in yourself—have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that been hard to come by lately?

Hi Sarah… I guess I can still laugh sometimes, but it definitely doesn’t come as easily as it used to. My sister sent me a silly video the other day and I chuckled, but most of the time I just feel kind of flat—like the joy gets buried under all the feeding, changing, and trying to keep the baby settled.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Most days I can still laugh a little—like when my husband makes a goofy face at the baby—but it feels muted, almost like I have to remind myself it’s okay to enjoy something.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still look forward to little things—like my mom bringing over dinner or taking the baby for a short walk—but the excitement isn’t as strong as it used to be. Sometimes I plan something I think I’ll enjoy, and then when it happens I just feel kind of “meh,” like the good feelings don’t fully show up.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that. Yesterday the baby was extra fussy and I kept thinking maybe it’s because I’m not soothing him right or my milk isn’t enough. I know, rationally, babies just have off days, but I still wonder if I missed something I should’ve done differently.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

I do feel anxious, pretty much every day—mostly about the baby. Like, I’ll lie down and suddenly worry that his breathing sounds different, or I’ll replay in my head whether I fastened the car-seat straps tightly enough. There’s not always a clear reason; the worry just shows up and my heart starts racing until I check on him again.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes I’ll be in the middle of folding laundry and suddenly feel this wave of panic—my chest gets tight, I can’t catch my breath, and I think something awful is about to happen. It passes after a few minutes, but it leaves me shaky and I don’t really know why it started in the first place.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days it feels like I’m treading water. I’ll finally get the baby down for a nap, turn to the sink full of bottles, and suddenly think, “I can’t keep up.” I’m not falling apart, but little tasks pile up and I feel this constant pressure that I’m one step behind.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

I wouldn’t say I’m miserable, but there are nights when my mind just won’t settle. I’ll lie there listening to every little sound the baby makes, or replay the day worrying I didn’t do enough, and then I’m awake for hours even when I’m exhausted. It probably happens three or four nights a week.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel sad some days—like this heaviness settles in and I can’t shake it. It’s not every moment, and I still have okay times, but the sadness pops up most evenings when things quiet down and I feel like I’m running on empty.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I haven’t cried much—maybe once or twice this week. It was late at night when the baby wouldn’t settle and I felt completely drained. The tears came for a minute, but they passed. It’s not a daily thing.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—nothing like that. I get overwhelmed and tired, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel like me again and be able to enjoy my baby.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 17: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening – 2 wks PP

Symptoms endorsed
- Persistent low mood, “heaviness,” evening worsening  
- Marked anhedonia (pleasure blunted, anticipatory enjoyment absent)  
- Daily free-floating anxiety, situational panic attacks (tight chest, breathlessness)  
- Excessive guilt / self-blame re infant care  
- Sleep initiation difficulty 3–4 nights/week (mood-related)  
- Subjective sense of being overwhelmed, “treading water”  
- Crying episodes 1–2×/week

Patterns
- Anxiety and low mood equally prominent  
- Symptoms interfere with daily functioning but no self-harm ideation

Risk factors / screening flags
- EPDS equivalent items: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 positive; item 10 negative  
- No suicidal or infanticidal thoughts reported

Screening impression
Moderate depressive and anxiety symptoms above normal postpartum adjustment; recommend formal assessment (EPDS, PHQ-9/GAD-7) and follow-up within 1–2 weeks, sooner if deterioration.
